TPRM SUBPAGE 02

Vendor Risk Tiering Matrix

Classify all vendors by inherent risk to determine due diligence depth, monitoring frequency, and contract requirements.

TPRM
\r\n

Used by TPRM Committee for vendor onboarding decisions and annual re-tiering.

\r\n

1. TIER DEFINITIONS

Vendor risk tiers

TierRisk levelDefinitionTypical profile
Tier 1HighProcesses sensitive PII, has administrative access to critical systems, or integrates with OT/IoT. A breach could cause material harm.Custom ERP/MES developers, AWS/Azure, payroll processors, OT integrators
Tier 2MediumProcesses limited PII or has restricted system access. Breach impact is moderate.SaaS CRM, logistics, IT support, analytics platforms
Tier 3LowNo PII access or only anonymized/aggregated data. Breach impact is minimal.Office supplies, training providers, non-PII consultants
\r\n

2. RISK SCORING MODEL (0-100)

Scoring dimensions

DimensionWeightScore 1: PoorScore 3: AdequateScore 5: Excellent
PII Exposure40%Sensitive PII at scale with admin accessLimited PII with restricted accessNo PII or anonymized only
Security Maturity30%No certifications or security programSOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001Multiple certifications and continuous improvement
Financial Stability10%Startup, no insurance, unclear financialsEstablished, insurance below $5MEnterprise-grade, insurance above $5M
Reputation & References20%Breaches, no references, legal actionsClean history and industry referencesExcellent reputation and thought leadership

Final Score = Sum of (Dimension Score x Weight)

\r\n

3. TIER ASSIGNMENT RULES

Approvals and overrides

0-40Tier 1 (High)CISO + Privacy Officer + Legal
41-70Tier 2 (Medium)CISO or delegate + Business Owner
71-100Tier 3 (Low)Business Owner

OVERRIDE RULES

Re-tier triggers

  • OT/IoT access+15 penalty
  • Offshore weak jurisdiction+10 penalty
  • Sole source critical functionFlag concentration risk
  • PII breach in 24 monthsAutomatic Tier 1
\r\n

4-6. CONTROL REQUIREMENTS

Due diligence, monitoring, and contracts

RequirementTier 1Tier 2Tier 3
Full due diligence questionnaireRequiredRequiredNot required
Technical assessmentRequiredIf PII involvedNot required
Reference checks3 or more2 or moreNot required
On-site / remote auditAnnual on-siteAnnual remoteTriennial or trigger-based
Security questionnaire refreshQuarterlyBiannualAnnual
DPA and audit rightsMandatoryIf PII / mandatory auditIf PII
Breach notificationWithin 48 hoursWithin 72 hoursIf PII
Cyber insurance$5M minimum$2M minimumNot required
\r\n

7-10. OPERATING REFERENCE

Re-tiering, manufacturing, register, and calculation

  • Re-tieringAnnual review, data scope change, PII incident, merger, regulation, or KPI deterioration
  • ManufacturingOT/IoT code, factory remote access, or biometrics normally adds +15 and likely Tier 1
  • RegisterVendor ID, name, service, four dimension scores, total, tier, last and next assessment

30%Security MaturityScore x 30

20%ReputationScore x 20

CYBERSECURITY GOVERNANCE

Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM)

Kelola risiko keamanan siber dari vendor, supplier, partner, dan pihak ketiga dalam satu ruang kerja.

TPRM
\r\n

RISK SCORING SYSTEM

Weighted TPRM risk summary

Total risk score = (Vendor Tier x 35%) + (CIA Risk Score x 40%) + (Related Risk Score x 25%).

35%Component A: Vendor TierTier 1 (High) = 100, Tier 2 (Medium) = 50, Tier 3 (Low) = 10.
40%Component B: CIA Risk ScoreUses the CIA score on a 0-100 scale. Lower CIA maturity scores produce higher risk contribution.
25%Component C: Related RiskVery Low = 1, Low = 2, Medium = 3, High = 4, Very High = 5.

RELATED RISK SUB-SCORE

Risk rating calculation

Sub-score = ((Very Low x 1) + (Low x 2) + (Medium x 3) + (High x 4) + (Very High x 5)) / (jumlah related risk x 5) x 100.

The summary is shown in color before the Actions column in the Third-party risk workspace.

\r\n

PURPOSE & SCOPE

Trusted partner governance

Framework ini mengatur vendor yang mengakses, memproses, atau mengembangkan sistem dengan data PII dan OT, termasuk software developer partners, SaaS, cloud, logistics, dan payroll providers.

GDPR Article 28CCPA Service ProviderPII & OT dataAudit readiness

POLICY OWNER

CISO + Procurement + Legal

Version 1.0 · Internal — Confidential

Review cadence: annual, dan setiap terjadi perubahan material pada vendor atau data flow.

\r\n

VENDOR LIFECYCLE

Four-phase control model

01

Selection & Due Diligence

Questionnaire, technical review, risk scoring, dan keputusan GO / NO-GO.

02

Contracting

DPA, audit rights, breach SLA, sub-processor approval, dan insurance.

03

Ongoing Monitoring

Quarterly reviews, annual audits, scorecard, KPI, dan escalation.

04

Offboarding

Data return/deletion, access revocation, certificate, dan post-termination audit.

\r\n

DUE DILIGENCE CRITERIA

Trusted software developer partner

  • CertificationsISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, atau equivalent
  • Security programSecurity Officer/DPO, incident response, breach SLA <= 48 hours
  • Manufacturing domainOT/IoT security, IEC 62443, industrial protocols
  • Secure developmentSAST, DAST, dependency scanning, OWASP Top 10
  • Financial stabilityCyber Liability Insurance >= $5M

RISK TIERING

Risk scoring model

0-40High Risk · Tier 1Enhanced due diligence, annual on-site audit, quarterly review, CISO approval
41-70Medium Risk · Tier 2Standard due diligence, annual remote audit, biannual review
71-100Low Risk · Tier 3Simplified due diligence, annual questionnaire, triennial audit
\r\n

SCOPE

In scope and out of scope

In scopeOut of scope
Software developers: custom ERP/MES, IoT platforms, analytics, cloudCommodity suppliers, unless they process PII
SaaS providers hosting or processing PIIOffice supplies and non-IT services
Cloud infrastructure providers such as AWS and AzureJanitorial/facilities, unless they access secure areas
Logistics partners receiving customer or shipping data
Payroll and HR processing vendors
Any vendor with logical or physical access to PII
\r\n

DUE DILIGENCE PROCESS

Questionnaire to GO / NO-GO

01

Vendor questionnaire

Self-attestation covering data processing, sub-processors, certifications, incidents, SDLC, and continuity.

02

Technical review

Validate evidence, penetration tests, vulnerability management, access controls, and architecture.

03

Risk scoring

Score PII exposure, security maturity, financial stability, and reputation from 0 to 100.

04

GO / NO-GO

Approve, reject, or require remediation and CISO approval before onboarding.

40%PII/Data ExposureVolume, sensitivity, access level, and data subject count
30%Security MaturityCertifications, pen tests, vulnerability program, incident history
10%Financial StabilityRevenue, years in business, and insurance coverage
20%Reputation & ReferencesClient references, public breaches, and legal actions

QUESTIONNAIRE

Minimum coverage

  • Data processingScope and sub-processor inventory
  • Security evidenceCertifications, audit history, and incidents
  • Secure SDLCRequired for software developers
  • ContinuityBusiness continuity and disaster recovery
\r\n

CONTRACTING

Required contractual provisions

ClauseRequirement / purposeReference
Data Processing Agreement (DPA)Mandatory for all PII processorsStandard DPA Template
Processing InstructionsOnly on documented instructions from CompanyGDPR Art. 28(3)(a)
CCPA Service ProviderNo sale/sharing; limited use; no data combinationCCPA Section 1798.140
Audit RightsAnnual and for-cause audit at Company discretion
Sub-Processor ApprovalPrior written consent and same DPA obligationsGDPR Art. 28(2)
Breach NotificationWithin 48 hours of discovery
Data Return/DeletionWithin 30 days; Certificate of Deletion required
Liability & IndemnificationVendor liable for breach fines, penalties, and remediation
International TransfersSCC/DPF incorporated where applicable
InsuranceCyber Liability minimum $5M per occurrence
\r\n

SOFTWARE DEVELOPER CLAUSES

Additional control requirements

  • Code Ownership & IPCompany retains custom code and derivative works
  • Backdoor ProhibitionNo undisclosed access, telemetry, or data exfiltration
  • Secure SDLCOWASP SAMM or equivalent with security gates
  • Code EscrowSource code escrow for critical systems
  • Developer AccessLeast privilege, session logs, background checks
  • Change ManagementPIA for changes affecting PII processing
\r\n

ONGOING MONITORING

Cadence, KPI, and escalation

ActivityTier 1 HighTier 2 MediumTier 3 Low
Security questionnaireQuarterlyBiannualAnnual
Evidence requestAnnualAnnualBiannual
On-site/Remote auditAnnual on-siteAnnual remoteTriennial
Performance reviewQuarterlyBiannualAnnual
Security scorecardContinuousContinuousNot required
Dark web / breach monitoringContinuousContinuousNot required

KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS

Required targets

  • Availability>= 99.9%
  • P1 response< 4 hours
  • P1 resolution< 24 hours
  • Unauthorized PII access0 events
  • Critical vulnerability< 48 hours
  • DSAR support< 5 business days

MONITORING TOOLS

Continuous monitoring

  • Security ratingsBitSight, SecurityScorecard
  • Threat intelligenceRecorded Future, Mandiant
  • Vendor risk platformOneTrust, ServiceNow GRC, ProcessUnity

OFFBOARDING

Triggers and checklist

  • TriggersTermination, non-renewal, bankruptcy, material DPA breach, or in-sourcing
  • Required actionsData export, access revocation, deletion certificate, monitoring removal
  • RetentionArchive contract, DPA, and records for 7 years
Day 0Notify vendorProcurement communicates return/deletion requirements
30 daysExport and deletionReceive data export and Certificate of Deletion
24 hoursRevoke accessRemove accounts, API keys, VPN, and repositories
6 monthsPost-termination auditRequired for Tier 1 vendors
\r\n
#Offboarding taskTimelineOwner
1Notify vendor of termination and data return/deletion requirementsDay 0Procurement

3Verify export completeness and integrityWithin 5 days of receiptIT + Business Owner

5Obtain Certificate of DeletionWithin 30 daysProcurement
6Verify deletion evidenceWithin 5 days of certificateIT Security
7Remove vendor from approved list and monitoring toolsWithin 5 daysTPRM Team
8Post-termination audit for Tier 1Within 6 monthsInternal Audit

\r\n

GOVERNANCE & ORGANIZATION

Roles and TPRM Committee

RoleResponsibility
CISOProgram owner, technical risk assessment, audit oversight
Privacy OfficerDPA compliance, RoPA entries, international transfers
ProcurementRFP, contract negotiation, financial due diligence
LegalDPA/contract review, liability, regulatory interpretation
IT SecurityTechnical assessment, monitoring, access management
Business OwnersVendor relationship, performance, renewal decisions
Internal AuditIndependent verification and annual effectiveness review

TPRM Committee bertemu setiap kuartal dengan agenda onboarding Tier 1/2, high-risk review, escalated issues, process improvement, renewals, dan offboarding.

\r\n

AUDIT, ROADMAP & REFERENCES

Implementation and standards

  • Annual IT AuditAudit sample Tier 1, exercise contract clauses, verify RoPA/data flows, assess effectiveness
  • Month 1-2Inventory vendors, obtain DPAs, tier risks, deploy questionnaire, train procurement
  • Month 3-4Renegotiate high-risk contracts and deploy monitoring dashboards
  • Month 5+Integrate annual audit cycle and launch TPRM Committee
  • OngoingQuarterly committee meetings and annual effectiveness review
  • ISO 27001 Annex A.15Supplier relationships
  • NIST SP 800-53 SASystem and Services Acquisition
  • NIST SP 800-161Supply Chain Risk Management
  • GDPR Art. 28Processor obligations
  • CCPA Section 1798.140Service Provider definition
  • SOC 2 CC7.2, CC9.2Vendor management trust criteria

Cybersecurity Risk Acceptance Form

Version 1.1

Cybersecurity risk acceptance is a deliberate executive decision by a business owner to acknowledge and accept a cybersecurity risk which, for the reason given, cannot be remediated through available security controls and measures.

Using this form, the application, service, or system owner describes the risk to be accepted, its potential impact, why it should be accepted, and mitigating factors, if any.
